messages.text: He risks his life to retrieve the letter because he is bored. That's only a proposed motive, not an established fact. Would that be enough to carry the sacrifice? Keep to one alternative if you suggest one.

Boredom alone would probably feel too slight to carry a deliberate risk to his life. It can explain why he becomes curious, but the reader needs to understand why getting this letter matters more to him than staying safe.

One alternative: he believes the letter offers a chance to put right a harm he caused. That gives the risk an emotional cost: walking away would mean leaving that harm unresolved.

Both motives remain proposals. The life-risking retrieval is also unestablished, and the earlier letter and childhood ideas stay undecided.
